question.problem:
Consider the function $f,$ defined as 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the shape of the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:R\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a scalar $x$ is the column vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂x}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times 1}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a scalar $x\in R,$ and

- outputs a vector $f(x)\in {R}^{2}.$

Therefore, the total derivative will be a column vector of shape $2\times 1.$
